messages.author: 6f5447e4bcccc657
messages.subject: A way summary() works
parts:
Dear Yves,

As a person trying to use lavaan within some automated analytical processes I've found it very inconvenient how summary() method for lavaan objects works. In R generally summary() returns an object (typically a list) that additionally has its own print() method to do this nice-loooking printing on the console (or other output stream). This approach allows convenient access to some typically useful informations, i.e. standard errors and signifficance of model parameters (compare: ```coef(lm(speed ~dist, cars))``` with ```coef(summary(lm(speed ~dist, cars)))```).

However in lavaan it seems, that this "two-stage" approach is not implemented. Summary() method do printing returninig nothing - so it does what its print() method can be supposed to do. And there is no easy way to obtain these nice tables that prints on the console as objects to be used for further operations within R.

So i wanted to ask whether it can be considered, to implement in lavaan this approach to returning (and printing) model summaries that is generally used in R.

Kind regards,

Tomek

parts: And there is no easy way to obtain these nice tables that prints on the console as objects to be used for further operations within R.

There is in the semTools package:

?clipboard
So i wanted to ask whether it can be considered, to implement in lavaan this approach to returning (and printing) model summaries that is generally used in R.

I recall my professor making the same observation about inconsistency with summary methods for other model objects in R.  I think the problem is that in SEM, there are so many things a researcher might be interested in summarizing (an issue partially handled by the idea of the inspect() method, see ?lavInspect for arguments).  The summary() method in lavaan is a fancy print() method because it just allows researchers to pick (salad-bar style) among the most commonly requested things.  See the class?lavaan help page for summary() arguments.  

If you are looking for anything that summary() prints, it can be found in other lavaan functions, corresponding to the summary() arguments: parameterEstimates(), standardizedSolution(), fitMeasures(), modIndices(), etc.
